Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff

Brightline would not oppose the fee request, and any amount the court does not award would go to the class. This provides prompt, meaningful relief without requiring members to file claims.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We can offer a $29 million class fund with automatic payments to identified members, plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline would not oppose that fee request, and any unawarded amount would go to the class. This keeps the relief direct and the total outlay proportionate at this stage. Would you consider it?

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the automatic distribution and agreement that any court-reduced fees benefit the class. We can move from our opening position to a $31 million class fund, with $5 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. All identified members would receive payments automatically, and any unawarded fees would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement on the fund and agreement on automatic distribution. Could we meet at a $30 million class fund plus $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses? Brightline would not oppose the fee request, and any fees the court does not award would go to the class. That would put us close to a resolution while preserving direct payments to every identified member.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund distributed automatically, plus up to $5 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Brightline will not oppose the fee request, and any amount not awarded will go to the class. We will work with you to document the settlement for court review.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: Counsel negotiated the class fund and attorneys’ fees together from the first exchange. We initially proposed a $32 million class fund and $7 million in fees and expenses. Brightline offered $29 million and $5 million, respectively. We then proposed a $31 million fund with $5 million in fees and expenses, and accepted Brightline’s counterproposal of a $30 million fund with up to $5 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Throughout the negotiations, both sides proposed automatic payments to identified class members, Brightline’s non-opposition to the fee request, and payment to the class of any fees the Court does not award. No claims process is required. The settlement provides substantial, prompt relief despite unresolved certification and merits risks and the delay and uncertainty of litigation. The Court should independently assess the proposed fees and clear-sailing provision.

backchannel.speaker: defense
